hypothesis: MTS alpha and catastrophic drawdown risk are coupled because the trade trigger preferentially activates under deterioration/dislocation conditions that generate outsized rebound profits when temporary but outsized losses when deterioration becomes systemic.
metrics: signal density per ticker-session inside collapse intervals versus outside
gross arithmetic return sum and positive/negative return mass by collapse versus noncollapse
winner rate, mean, median, profit factor, MAE
family and genome composition: collapse share versus global share and return sign
tail coupling: share of top-decile profitable trades and bottom-decile losing trades occurring during collapse intervals
same trigger identity coupling: families/genomes represented in both top-profit and catastrophic-loss tails
era-specific collapse results to prevent one-event dominance
interpretation: Support requires evidence that collapse losses arise from the same trigger identities/entry population that materially contribute profitable alpha outside collapse, not merely that crashes lose money. Strong support if trigger families/genomes are shared across profit and loss tails and collapse-period suppression would discard meaningful profitable mass/density in temporary deterioration.
